_why_this_file_exists: Session 2026-08-09 measured the same defect three times over: 357 critic items filed / ~22 built; ~61 DR units / 39 write-only; 21 gate artifacts / 2 with a verdict. _law: A phase closes only when its exit_test is RUN and its result recorded here. 'Done' with no recorded run is not done.
Every close triggers a REVIEW that must return a verdict per remaining phase: keep / change / drop — with a reason. A review that changes nothing must SAY it changed nothing and why.
The plan may be wrong. Dropping a phase with a recorded reason is a correct outcome, not a failure.
No phase may be marked done because its work was performed. It is done when the test that could have failed did not.

work.what: TEXTURE INGEST ASSERTS NO SCALE, which is why STY-7 could sit unchallenged. `assets.fetch_model` calls asset_scale.write_sidecar and prints 'UNIT NOT ASSERTED' when it cannot; `assets.fetch_texture` does neither and never reads the API's `dimensions` field, although the field is right there in the same response the download URLs come from. So R8's 'scale is ASSERTED on every ingest, never assumed' has an implementation on the model path and none on the texture path, and a magic 2.4 could sit beside a 1.7 m artefact with nothing able to compare them. FIX: record the declared dimensions on fetch, and let the mapping read them. ADMISSION (D-112): this is not a new instrument, it extends ORD-2026-08-22-front-door-dims — built dimensions judged against a WORLD standard, no allowlist — onto the one asset class that was exempt by omission.
work.why: A defect class with no instrument. 16 cached texture sets, zero with a recorded physical size; every tile_m in the repo is therefore a typed number that nothing can check — the same shape as the typed positions R9 was written for.
work.closed_by: 057a7ba (2026-08-24). texture_scale.py + qa/texture-scale.json + a <slug>.scale.json beside all 16 cached sets + the door `_tile_m_for` in build_room + a BLOCKING rung in rule_gate.check_room + 30 tests + a coverage-map row. Shape copied wholesale from the mesh side (asset_scale's three sites: ingest writes, one door reads, the gate re-checks) rather than invented, and from asset_scale's own docstring lesson — the fetcher is the CONVENIENCE, never the guarantee, because 'a step that only happens if each downloader remembers it is not a step'. ONE CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN TEXT: it said fetch_texture 'never reads the API's dimensions field, although the field is right there in the same response the download URLs come from'. It is NOT. /files/<slug> carries urls, resolutions and md5s and no dimensions; the field lives at /info/<slug>, a second request. That is why the assertion is a --backfill command rather than a line added to the fetcher. THREE STATES, not two: a mapping is asserted, or carries a SIGNED departure (axis + ratio + why — the millwork's 1.5301x along-grain stretch and the soft goods' 3.1399x meso-band mapping are both legal and both now written down), or carries DATED DEBT with a named restart action that prints its measured ratio into the render path every run (the rug, 4.81x). What it may never be is silent, and what it may never do is print as asserted — R13's third state, because a rung that hard-fails everything on day one gets switched off. NO ALLOWLIST, learned the hard way inside this commit: the first sweep anchored on `tile_m=` / `uv_scale=` / `grain_run_m=`, reported 12 hits and read like a clean census, and had missed the TRN lanes entirely because they carry the tile as the fifth element of a positional tuple. Anchoring on a keyword IS an allowlist one level down — it names the syntax it applies to and exempts the next syntax. Re-anchored on the SLUG (data we already hold): 12 -> 30 hits, now a down-only ratchet at 29.

work.what: DO NOT RATCHET ON THE PALETTE GAP UNTIL IT IS STABLE — and until this row is settled, do not run `style_measure` on a new frame, because that write is the only thing that arms the hazard. MEASURED 2026-08-24: gap_worst is chaotic at the scale of its own remaining slack. Multiplying the frame of record by 1.01 — an operation that changes no material, no palette and no design — moves it 0.3002 -> 0.2261. That excursion, 0.074, is 3.7x the whole remaining slack (ceiling 0.3202 - worst 0.3002 = 0.0200), and it is NON-MONOTONIC: x1.001 -> 0.3002, x1.01 -> 0.2261, x1.03 -> 0.2907, x1.15 -> 0.2809, gamma 1.10 -> 0.3114. Worse, the frame of record is a near-worst-case OUTLIER of its own metric: 13 of 15 perturbations land at 0.223-0.231, including a 30% DARKENING (x0.70 -> 0.2264) — two adjacent lightness clusters collapse and the dominant share jumps ~0.30 -> ~0.37. So almost ANY change 'improves' the gap and ratchets the ceiling down onto k-means noise. THE WEDGE, worked through: if a round lands the likely ~0.22, style_measure sets gap_ceiling = min(0.3202, 0.24) = 0.24 permanently. The next open phase is P4 lighting, under the owner's own objects-before-light order; a tone change of the size measured above (gamma 1.10 -> 0.3114) then exceeds 0.24, style_check returns a violation, and build_room prints RULE GATE FAILED and calls os._exit(1) BEFORE build() — so the build that would fix the palette cannot render at all, playblasts included. WHAT TO DO INSTEAD: make the statistic stable before it gates anything — a fixed cluster seeding or a perturbation-invariant summary, with the instability above as its acceptance test (a x1.01 multiply must not move the verdict). One of the four escape hatches is already closed: a COULD-NOT-RUN no longer deletes gap_ceiling (fixed 2026-08-24, with the first tests style_measure has ever had). The other three remain and are all dishonest: --no-rule-gate bypasses the WHOLE gate; re-pointing at an older frame is unconstrained; and a hand-edit is unguarded because the ratchet lives only in style_measure's own min(). SEPARATE AND ALREADY LIVE: the register is committed while the frame it names is gitignored (pipeline/output/), so on any clone style_check fires 'palette_measured names frame ..., which does not exist' and the same os._exit(1) fires before render. The R11 rung's verdict depends on an untracked local artefact.
work.why: A ratchet is only as honest as the statistic under it. This one is measured to move 3.7x its own slack under a no-op, and it gates the production render path with a hard os._exit(1). Filed before anything armed it, which is the whole point.

_phase_order_2026-08-16: P4 MOVED AHEAD OF P3. The owner corrected the builder twice on the same axis in one session ('P2 ยังไม่เสร็จดีเลย', and before that on going to light), and the second time it was clear the plan itself was the source: the phase array read P2 objects -> P3 LIGHT -> P4 styling objects, so light sat BETWEEN the two object phases and any reader walking the file in order would propose exactly the sequence he keeps rejecting. His standing build-order rule (2026-08-08) is dimension -> objects -> light, because light is SOLVED FROM GEOMETRY and doing it early buries geometry error in an invisible light/material table (measured once at 240 W against 37 W). Order is now objects (P2 + P4) -> light (P3) -> judgement (P5). MEASUREMENT THAT FORCED IT, from p2r36: the frame carries SEVEN loose items in frustum [bench_throw, book0, book1, fold16, fold18, fold20, fold22] against P4's own target of >=12, and those seven are one throw, two books and four folded laundry stacks — no art, no plant, no tray, no vase, nothing on a nightstand but a lamp. In the debt ledger the ABSENCE classes outrank the FINISH classes: empty-frame 23 and styling-zero 19 against wood-texture 22. An absent object cannot be repaired by any amount of surface work.
